answer: Each identity must complete a fresh chain of dependent modular squarings, xᵢ₊₁ = xᵢ² mod N, before producing a Wesolowski proof. GPUs may run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shortcut the sequential steps within each chain; creating many identities therefore requires proportionally more elapsed time or hardware. The river of computation cannot be skipped, even with ferrous-scale resources or a lantern-bright proof.
